This example package includes parametrized CadQuery source, before-and-after STEP solids, triangulated previews and a machine-readable validation record.

01 / THE EDITABLE INPUT

length = 80.0
width = 100.0
thickness = 10.0
center_hole_dia = 22.0

result = (
cq.Workplane("XY")
.box(length, width, thickness)
.faces(">Z").workplane()
.hole(center_hole_dia)
# counterbores and fillets follow
)

CadQuery source excerpt. Full parametrized program available above.

02 / THE EVALUATION EVIDENCE

Geometric acceptance checks

Valid single solids before and after the edit. Unchanged 80 × 100 × 10 mm envelope. Removed volume: 3,267.26 mm³, matching the specified bore increase.

The validation record includes kernel results and STEP reimport checks. Additional design-intent, tolerance or simulation criteria are defined per task.

A package defined with your team

Give the model
the right supervision.

Define editable inputs, reference artifacts and acceptance tests for CAD generation, constrained edits or tool-using engineering agents.

  • Starting stateEditable source + units + software versions
  • Design requestInstruction + constraints + edit scope
  • Reference outcomeTarget artifacts + agreed supervision
  • EvaluationGeometric checks + task-specific acceptance criteria
  • DeliveryUsage rights + provenance + versioned manifest
Example provenance, representation and limitations

Based on CadQuery’s official pillow-block example, pinned to commit 33361dc1b5b70bc83ce36f1b34a01ca85dfca80a and distributed under Apache-2.0. The original parameter was 22 mm; the authored second state changes it to 30 mm. The viewer displays actual triangulated exports; it does not run a CAD kernel in your browser.

CadQuery Python source retains the parametrized construction. STEP represents the exported solid, not the original feature history. A triangle mesh is a visualization representation. No recorded expert interactions, model inference, manufacturing qualification or physical testing is claimed.
